title: Assistant Controller
description:
Assistant Controller
Accounting Operations | Financial Close | Controls & Compliance
 
 
Location
Newport Beach / Orange County, California
Employment Type
Full-time
Department
Finance
Reports To
Dan Hejza, VP of Finance / Controller
Compensation
150,000–200,000 base salary, plus bonus, equity, and benefits
About Tiberius Aerospace
Tiberius Aerospace is a cutting-edge aerospace and defense company delivering advanced, mission-critical technologies for government and private-sector customers. We develop high-performance aerospace systems, secure engineering solutions, and complex hardware built for demanding operational environments.
Tiberius is scaling quickly and is seeking finance leaders who bring rigor, ownership, and operational discipline to a fast-moving hardware business. Our finance team is a strategic partner to the organization—building the systems, controls, and insight required to support growth while maintaining the standards expected of a high-consequence aerospace and defense company.
The Role
Tiberius Aerospace is seeking an experienced and hands-on Assistant Controller to help build, manage, and scale the company’s accounting function.
Reporting directly to Dan Hejza, VP of Finance / Controller, this role will own critical elements of the monthly and annual close process, general-ledger integrity, financial reporting, internal controls, and day-to-day accounting operations. The Assistant Controller will work closely with leaders across Finance, Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, People, Legal, and Program Management to ensure accurate financial information, disciplined processes, and timely decision support.
This is a deliberate succession-track role. The successful candidate will have the technical rigor, operating judgment, and leadership ability to take on increasing ownership of the accounting organization and transition into the Controller role within several quarters based on performance.
The ideal candidate is equally comfortable working at the detail level—reconciling accounts, reviewing journal entries, and resolving close issues—as they are improving processes, developing accounting policies, supporting audits, building a team, and creating scalable financial infrastructure.
What You’ll Do
Accounting Operations & Financial Close
Lead key components of the monthly, quarterly, and annual financial-close process, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and timeliness.
Maintain the integrity of the general ledger, including account reconciliations, journal entries, accruals, prepaids, fixed assets, intercompany activity, and other balance-sheet accounts.
Review journal entries, reconciliations, supporting schedules, and close deliverables prepared by internal team members and external accounting partners.
Prepare and review monthly financial statements, management reporting packages, flux analyses, and supporting schedules.
Drive timely resolution of accounting discrepancies, unusual transactions, balance-sheet issues, and close-related risks.
Establish and maintain close calendars, standard operating procedures, account-ownership structures, and documentation standards.
Support cash-management, banking, treasury, and payment-control activities as needed.
Financial Reporting, Controls & Compliance
Support the preparation of accurate and timely financial reporting in accordance with U.S. GAAP.
Develop, document, and strengthen accounting policies, internal controls, and finance procedures appropriate for a scaling aerospace and defense organization.
Maintain a strong internal-control environment across accounting processes, including procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, payroll, inventory, fixed assets, expense reporting, and financial close.
Support external audit, tax, lender, diligence, and other compliance requests by preparing schedules, documentation, and technical accounting support.
Assist with the implementation of new accounting standards, policy updates, and technical accounting analyses.
Identify control gaps, operational risks, and process inefficiencies; design practical solutions and drive adoption across the business.
Support compliance with applicable government-contracting, defense-industry, export-control, and record-retention requirements as they affect finance operations.
Inventory, Cost Accounting & Operational Finance
Partner with Operations, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Program Management to ensure accurate accounting for inventory, work in process, standard costs, purchase commitments, and capital assets.
Support the development and maintenance of cost-accounting processes for complex hardware, engineering development, prototype builds, and production programs.
Review inventory reserves, obsolescence, capitalization policies, fixed-asset records, and depreciation schedules.
Help improve visibility into material costs, labor, overhead, manufacturing variances, and program-level financial performance.
Support accounting and reporting for government contracts, customer programs, milestone-based activity, and revenue-recognition considerations as applicable.
Assist in building the processes and controls needed to scale from development programs into repeatable production operations.
Systems, Process Improvement & Team Leadership
Help optimize the company’s ERP, expense-management, procurement, financial-reporting, and close-management systems.
Drive automation and process improvement across recurring accounting workflows, reporting, reconciliations, and approvals.
Partner with FP&A to ensure actuals, forecasts, budgets, and operating metrics are aligned and reliably reported.
Support, mentor, and develop accounting team members as the function grows.
Serve as a trusted finance partner to functional leaders, explaining financial results, policies, controls, and risks clearly and practically.
Participate in cross-functional projects, systems implementations, financing activities, acquisition diligence, and other strategic initiatives as needed.
What You’ll Bring
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
Active CPA license required.
8+ years of progressive accounting experience, including public-accounting experience at a Big Four firm in audit, assurance, transaction services, or a related accounting-advisory practice.
Demonstrated experience in a high-growth startup or scaling technology, aerospace, defense, manufacturing, hardware, or other operationally complex environment.
Proven ownership of core accounting operations, including month-end close, financial reporting, general ledger, reconciliations, internal controls, audit readiness, and process improvement.
Experience operating in an environment where processes, systems, and organizational structure are still being built—not simply maintained.
Strong command of U.S. GAAP, financial-statement preparation, accounting-policy development, and balance-sheet management.
Experience with inventory, fixed assets, accruals, cost accounting, or manufacturing accounting.
Demonstrated ability to build, lead, mentor, or materially upgrade an accounting team.
Advanced Excel skills and comfort working within ERP and financial-reporting systems.
Ability to operate effectively in an evolving environment, establish structure where it does not yet exist, and balance urgency with sound financial judgment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across finance and non-finance teams.
High integrity, sound judgment, discretion, and a strong ownership mentality.
Clear potential to assume the Controller role within several quarters based on demonstrated execution, leadership capability, technical-accounting depth, and ability to scale the accounting function.
U.S. Person status, due to access requirements for export-controlled information and facilities.
Preferred Qualifications
Prior experience as an Assistant Controller, Accounting Manager, Senior Accounting Manager, or Controller within a high-growth or scaling company.
Experience supporting audit readiness, external financial-statement audits, due diligence, financing activity, or board reporting.
Experience with aerospace, defense, government contracting, project accounting, or manufacturing operations.
Familiarity with cost-accounting methods, inventory valuation, standard costing, and manufacturing variance analysis.
Experience implementing or optimizing an ERP system, including NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics, SAP, Oracle, or similar platforms.
Experience building accounting policies, procedures, control matrices, and finance-process documentation.
Familiarity with FAR, CAS, DCAA, government-contracting, or defense-finance requirements.
Prior people-management and team-development experience.
What Success Looks Like
Within the first several months, you will establish yourself as a reliable owner of the close process and a trusted partner to Dan Hejza, VP of Finance / Controller, and the broader finance organization. The accounting team will have clearer ownership, stronger reconciliations, more disciplined documentation, and a predictable close cadence.
You will demonstrate the ability to lead a reliable and increasingly efficient financial close; improve the integrity and timeliness of financial reporting; strengthen accounting policies and controls; and build credibility with functional leaders, auditors, lenders, and senior leadership.
Over time, you will help build an accounting function that delivers timely, accurate, audit-ready information; supports operational decision-making; and scales alongside Tiberius’s engineering, manufacturing, and program execution.
Growth Opportunity
This is a deliberate Controller succession-track opportunity. The Assistant Controller will work directly with Dan Hejza, VP of Finance / Controller, taking on meaningful ownership of the accounting function from the outset.
The successful candidate should be prepared to demonstrate the technical rigor, leadership maturity, operational judgment, and cross-functional credibility required to step into the Controller role within several quarters. Progression will be based on execution—not tenure—including the ability to lead a reliable close, strengthen controls, build a high-performing accounting team, support audit and reporting requirements, and establish scalable finance infrastructure for Tiberius’s next stage of growth.
Compensation & Benefits
Tiberius Aerospace offers a 150,000–150,000–200,000 base salary, plus bonus eligibility, equity participation, comprehensive health benefits, and a 401(k). Final compensation will be determined based on experience, technical depth, leadership capability, and the needs of the business.

title: Capture Manager
description:
About Tiberius Aerospace
Tiberius Aerospace is a cutting-edge Aerospace and Defense company committed to delivering innovative, secure, and compliant solutions for our customers. We specialize in mission-critical technology services for government and private sector customers, ensuring excellence in aerospace systems design, performance, and compliance. To serve our nations with Strength, Honor, and Purpose - forging the systems that defend freedom and shape the future of defense.


Position Overview
 
Tiberius is seeking an experienced Capture Manager to lead the pursuit of strategic opportunities across the Department of Defense and Intelligence Community, from early identification through contract award.
 
This is a high-ownership role for someone who thrives before the RFP drops building customer relationships, shaping requirements, running competitive intelligence, and assembling the win strategy that turns an early lead into a program of record. The Capture Manager will work closely with the cofounders, business development, engineering, and program teams to convert Tiberius's technical capability into funded, winnable pursuits.
 
The ideal candidate has run capture campaigns inside DoD or IC acquisition environments, understands how programs of record actually get built, and can operate with the pace and informality of a startup while speaking fluently to program offices, primes, and government stakeholders.
 
 
What You'll Do
 
Own capture strategy and execution for strategic pursuits across DoD and IC customers, from early qualification through award
Identify, qualify, and prioritize opportunities aligned with Tiberius's programs and technical roadmap, including bid/no-bid recommendations to leadership
Build and execute capture plans: customer engagement strategy, win themes, competitive positioning, teaming approach, and price-to-win input
Build and maintain relationships with program office, requirements, and acquisition stakeholders ahead of formal solicitations
Run competitive intelligence track incumbents, likely competitors, past performance, and pricing patterns to shape a winning position
Identify and negotiate teaming relationships with primes, subcontractors, and industry partners where capability gaps exist
Partner with engineering and program teams to translate customer requirements into a compelling, technically credible solution
Support proposal development: shape win themes, review compliance, and contribute to proposal sections as needed
Track and report pursuit status, pipeline, and capture milestones through the CRM, in partnership with the RevOps Manager
Represent Tiberius at industry days, technical forums, and customer engagements
 
Capture Process & Competitive Strategy
 
Lead gate reviews (qualify, pursue, propose, submit) with clear go/no-go criteria and executive sign-off
Develop win themes and discriminators grounded in Tiberius's actual technical differentiation, not generic value props
Coordinate black-hat and competitive assessment sessions ahead of major pursuits
Maintain a live capture pipeline with accurate stage, value, probability, and next-action data
Work with contracts and finance on pricing strategy and cost-realism for major pursuits
 
What You'll Bring
 
5+ years of capture management experience in DoD or IC acquisition environments
Demonstrated track record of shaping and winning defense programs, from early-stage pursuits through program of record 
Strong understanding of DoD/IC acquisition pathways: FAR/DFARS, OTAs, SBIR/STTR, MTA, IDIQ, and program-of-record transitions 
Experience building and negotiating teaming agreements with primes, subs, and industry partners 
Excellent relationship-building skills across government, industry, and internal technical stakeholders 
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including comfort presenting to senior government and executive audiences 
Comfortable operating in a fast-paced startup environment with minimal structure, building process as you go 
 
Preferred
 
Prior military service or direct experience supporting a DoD or IC program office
Active or recent TS/SCI clearance, or eligibility to obtain one
Experience capturing opportunities in fires, precision munitions, autonomy, or related weapons-systems domains
APMP Capture Practitioner Certification or equivalent
Experience at an early-stage or high-growth defense-tech company, not only a traditional prime
Familiarity with Salesforce or a comparable CRM for pipeline tracking
 
What We're Looking For
 
A relationship-first operator who builds trust with program offices long before an RFP exists
Someone who can hold both the big picture (program-of-record strategy) and the granular (teaming agreements, pricing input, proposal compliance)
A collaborative leader who can pull engineering, program, and executive stakeholders into a single pursuit without needing formal authority to do it
Comfortable being the first Capture Manager in the building 
Bias for action balanced with the discipline to walk away from a bad-fit pursuit
 
Growth Opportunity
 
This role provides the opportunity to build the capture function for a rapidly growing aerospace and defense company from the ground up, working directly with the cofounders to convert Tiberius's technical roadmap into a funded pipeline of programs of record.

title: CFD Engineer
description:
CFD Engineer – Aerodynamics &
Propulsion
High-Fidelity Simulation | Internal & External Flows | Inlet, Combustor & Nozzle Analysis
Job Title CFD Engineer – Aerodynamics & Propulsion
Location Hybrid; remote considered for the right candidate
Employment Type Full Time
Department Engineering / Aerodynamics & Propulsion
Reports To Shawn Gilmore
Salary Range $100,000 to $150,000
Equity Yes
About Tiberius Aerospace
Tiberius Aerospace is a cutting-edge Aerospace and Defense company delivering advanced, mission-critical
technologies for government and private sector customers. The company focuses on high-performance
aerospace systems, secure engineering solutions, and the development of complex hardware built for demanding
operational environments. Tiberius is scaling quickly and is looking for engineers who can operate with
ownership, urgency, and technical discipline in a high-stakes environment.
Position Overview
Tiberius Aerospace is seeking a CFD Engineer to support aerodynamic and propulsion analysis for our advanced
air vehicle and munition programs. This role is hands-on with the simulation stack: meshing, solving, and post-
processing high-fidelity CFD for internal flows (inlets, combustors, nozzles) and external aerodynamics across
subsonic through high-supersonic regimes. You will work closely with aerodynamics and propulsion engineers to
turn design questions into well-posed CFD studies and turn CFD results into design guidance the rest of the team
can use. This is an excellent role for an engineer who wants deep, hands-on computational experience on real
flight hardware programs.
What You'll Do
Set up, solve, and post-process high-fidelity CFD simulations for internal flows including inlets, combustors, and
nozzles, and external aerodynamic flows across the flight envelope.
Support inlet and nozzle flow path design studies using high-fidelity RANS or transient CFD as appropriate to the
design phase.
Generate aerodynamic and propulsion databases from CFD results for use in vehicle performance modeling and
trajectory simulation.
Develop and execute large-scale parametric CFD studies on commercial or government high-performance
computing platforms.
Support combustor and reacting-flow analysis workflows including fuel injection, atomization, and combustion
process modeling as applicable to the propulsion architecture.
Correlate CFD predictions against wind tunnel, direct-connect, or flight test data and help refine simulation setup
based on observed discrepancies.
Document CFD methodology, mesh and solver settings, and validation basis for each major analysis campaign.

Collaborate with the Aero-Propulsion and Flight Dynamics & Controls teams to ensure CFD-derived data products
meet the fidelity and format requirements of downstream simulation users.
CFD Methods & Simulation Execution
Develop and refine computational meshes for internal and external flow domains, balancing mesh resolution
against turnaround time requirements for each phase of design.
Configure and run RANS and, where required, transient high-fidelity CFD simulations (such as DES or DDES) for
inlet and combustor performance, nozzle flow, and external aerodynamic characterization.
Apply viscous-coupled panel methods or method-of-characteristics tools for rapid conceptual-level aerodynamic
design studies ahead of higher-fidelity CFD confirmation.
Post-process CFD results to extract performance metrics such as pressure recovery, distortion, thrust and drag
bookkeeping, and aerodynamic coefficients, and package results into formats usable by the performance
modeling and trajectory simulation teams.
Support reacting-flow CFD setup for combustor analysis, including fuel injection and atomization modeling,
working under the direction of propulsion engineers.
Manage CFD job submission, monitoring, and data management on HPC platforms, troubleshooting convergence
issues and solver stability problems as they arise.
Support correlation studies comparing CFD predictions to wind tunnel, ground test, and flight test data, helping
identify and document sources of discrepancy.
Maintain CFD case documentation including mesh generation procedures, boundary condition definitions, solver
settings, and convergence criteria for reproducibility and audit.
Operational & Cross-Functional Support
Coordinate with Aero-Propulsion team members on CFD study scope, priority, and turnaround requirements
relative to program design milestones.
Provide aerodynamic and propulsion data products to the Flight Dynamics & Controls team for trajectory
simulation and stability analysis use.
Support test planning activities by providing pre-test CFD predictions used to define wind tunnel or ground test
points and success criteria.
Participate in design reviews and provide CFD-based technical support for aerodynamic and propulsion design
decisions.
Coordinate with IT or computing infrastructure support on HPC account access, software licensing, and
computational resource allocation.
Support documentation of CFD methodology and results for program milestone review packages.
What You'll Bring
B.S. or higher in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.
2 to 5 years of CFD experience, which may include relevant graduate research, internships, or industry
experience on air vehicle, propulsion, or munition programs.
Hands-on experience with at least one major CFD solver (e.g., commercial codes such as Fluent or STAR-CCM+,
or DoD/academic codes such as FUN3D, Kestrel, or CFD++).
Working knowledge of meshing tools and mesh generation strategies for internal and external aerodynamic flow
domains.
Understanding of compressible aerodynamics and propulsion flow physics across subsonic through high-
supersonic regimes.
Proficiency in CFD post-processing, data reduction, and automation.
Must be a U.S. citizen and eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.

Preferred Experience
Experience with internal flow CFD for inlets, combustors, or nozzles on air-breathing propulsion systems.
Experience with reacting-flow or combustion CFD modeling.
Familiarity with transient high-fidelity methods such as DES, DDES, or LES for operability and distortion analysis.
Experience running CFD on commercial or DoD HPC platforms, including job scheduling and parallel scaling.
Background correlating CFD predictions against wind tunnel, ground test, and flight test data.
Experience with high-dynamic, high-g, or gun-launched flight environments.
Active or clearable to obtain a U.S. government security clearance.
What We're Looking For
A CFD engineer who is genuinely comfortable in the weeds of a simulation — mesh quality, boundary conditions,
convergence behavior — and who can troubleshoot a stalled solver without escalating every issue.
Someone who understands that a CFD result is only useful if it is correctly framed, documented, and handed off
in a format the next person can actually use.
An engineer who is eager to grow technical depth in propulsion integration and flight vehicle aerodynamics, with
strong fundamentals and the right instincts to build on.
Someone who communicates results clearly, flags uncertainty honestly, and is comfortable saying when a result
does not look right rather than passing along a number without scrutiny.
A team player who enjoys working closely with a senior lead, absorbing methodology, and taking on increasing
analysis ownership over time.
Compensation & Benefits
Tiberius Aerospace offers competitive base compensation commensurate with experience, equity participation,
comprehensive health benefits, and 401(k). Specific compensation will be discussed during the interview process.
Growth Opportunity
This role offers the opportunity to build deep, hands-on CFD expertise on real flight hardware programs, working
directly with Aero-Propulsion colleagues on propulsion integration and vehicle aerodynamics for next-generation
precision strike systems. As Tiberius scales through Series A and into full-rate development, this person will have
the opportunity to take on increasing analysis ownership, lead CFD studies independently, and grow into a senior
aerodynamics or propulsion engineering role.

Generate aerodynamic and propulsion databases from CFD results for use in vehicle performance modeling and

trajectory simulation.

Develop and execute large-scale parametric CFD studies on commercial or government high-performance

computing platforms.

Support combustor and reacting-flow analysis workflows including fuel injection, atomization, and combustion

process modeling as applicable to the propulsion architecture.

Correlate CFD predictions against wind tunnel, direct-connect, or flight test data and help refine simulation setup

based on observed discrepancies.

Document CFD methodology, mesh and solver settings, and validation basis for each major analysis campaign.

Collaborate with the Aero-Propulsion and Flight Dynamics & Controls teams to ensure CFD-derived data products

Develop and refine computational meshes for internal and external flow domains, balancing mesh resolution

against turnaround time requirements for each phase of design.

Configure and run RANS and, where required, transient high-fidelity CFD simulations (such as DES or DDES) for

Apply viscous-coupled panel methods or method-of-characteristics tools for rapid conceptual-level aerodynamic

Post-process CFD results to extract performance metrics such as pressure recovery, distortion, thrust and drag

bookkeeping, and aerodynamic coefficients, and package results into formats usable by the performance

modeling and trajectory simulation teams.

Support reacting-flow CFD setup for combustor analysis, including fuel injection and atomization modeling,

Manage CFD job submission, monitoring, and data management on HPC platforms, troubleshooting convergence

issues and solver stability problems as they arise.

Support correlation studies comparing CFD predictions to wind tunnel, ground test, and flight test data, helping

identify and document sources of discrepancy.

Maintain CFD case documentation including mesh generation procedures, boundary condition definitions, solver

settings, and convergence criteria for reproducibility and audit.

Operational & Cross-Functional Support

Coordinate with Aero-Propulsion team members on CFD study scope, priority, and turnaround requirements

relative to program design milestones.

Provide aerodynamic and propulsion data products to the Flight Dynamics & Controls team for trajectory

Support test planning activities by providing pre-test CFD predictions used to define wind tunnel or ground test

Participate in design reviews and provide CFD-based technical support for aerodynamic and propulsion design

B.S. or higher in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.

2 to 5 years of CFD experience, which may include relevant graduate research, internships, or industry

Hands-on experience with at least one major CFD solver (e.g., commercial codes such as Fluent or STAR-CCM+,

Working knowledge of meshing tools and mesh generation strategies for internal and external aerodynamic flow

Understanding of compressible aerodynamics and propulsion flow physics across subsonic through high-

Proficiency in CFD post-processing, data reduction, and automation.

Background correlating CFD predictions against wind tunnel, ground test, and flight test data.

Active or clearable to obtain a U.S. government security clearance.

Interface with government customer technical representatives and subject matter experts on performance

Experience working with test data including data reduction, basic statistical analysis, and uncertainty
considerations.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail in maintaining models, databases, and analysis documentation.
Must be a U.S. citizen and eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.
Preferred Experience
Experience reducing flight test, wind tunnel, direct-connect engine, or ground engine test data.
Experience supporting test planning including instrumentation definition and test point selection.
Background in uncertainty quantification or statistical analysis methods applied to engineering performance data.
Experience with high-dynamic, high-g, or gun-launched flight environments.

A technically credible presenter who can stand in front of a customer at a CDR and defend a performance

Full Time

About Tiberius Aerospace
Tiberius Aerospace is a cutting-edge Aerospace and Defense company delivering advanced, mission-critical technologies for government and private sector customers. The company focuses on high-performance aerospace systems, secure engineering solutions, and the development of complex hardware built for demanding operational environments. Tiberius is scaling quickly and is looking for engineers who can operate with ownership, urgency, and technical discipline in a high-stakes environment.
Position Overview
Tiberius Aerospace is seeking a Senior GNC Navigation Engineer to own the translation of GNC algorithms into production-grade, real-time embedded flight software for the program. This role bridges algorithm design and hardware, developing the embedded navigation filter, guidance logic, and autopilot control laws on the flight computer, along with the SIL and HIL infrastructure required to verify GNC performance end-to-end from algorithm through silicon. You are the person who makes the math run in the box.
What You'll Do
Implement GNC algorithms including the navigation filter, guidance law, and autopilot control laws in embedded C or C++ targeting the flight computer.
Define and own the GNC flight software architecture including task scheduling, sensor data interfaces, GNC state machine, and fault detection logic.
Develop and maintain the Software-in-the-Loop environment integrating GNC flight code with the 6-DOF trajectory simulation for closed-loop algorithm verification.
Design and build the Hardware-in-the-Loop test bench including GPS signal stimulation, IMU stimulation hardware, actuator emulation, and avionics bus interfaces.
Apply and enforce flight software coding standards and institute code review processes across the GNC software team.
Define GNC software requirements and verification test cases and execute and close the GNC software V&V test plan.
Collaborate with navigation and controls engineers on algorithm translation, numerical stability, and fixed and floating-point performance trade-offs.
Perform real-time performance characterization covering CPU budget, worst-case execution time, timing jitter, and latency analysis.
Support environmental test, ground test, and range test activities as the GNC software technical lead.
Technical & Algorithm Implementation & Flight Software Engineering
Implement the GPS/INS navigation filter in embedded C or C++ with rigorous attention to numerical stability, fixed-point arithmetic constraints, and real-time execution timing.
Develop the GNC task framework including sensor read scheduling, filter update cadence, guidance computation, and actuator command output with deterministic timing.
Build and maintain the SIL environment in which the production GNC flight binary executes against the MATLAB/Simulink 6-DOF plant model in closed loop for regression testing.
Design the HIL test bench architecture including interface hardware for GPS receiver simulation, IMU digital output stimulation, actuator feedback emulation, and data recording.
Implement auto-code generation workflow from MATLAB/Simulink navigation and control law models to production C code using Embedded Coder or equivalent.
Define and apply coding standards for the GNC software module including MISRA-C rules, static analysis requirements, and unit test coverage expectations.
Develop the GNC software build system, regression test suite, and continuous integration process to support rapid algorithm iteration.
Characterize flight computer GNC software performance under worst-case loading and document CPU margin, memory usage, and stack depth results.
Operational & Engineering Support
Interface with the flight computer hardware team on processor selection, memory architecture, sensor bus protocols, and boot sequence requirements.
Coordinate GNC software schedule and deliverables with systems engineering, the navigation team, and the I&T team.
Support range test activities by providing GNC software configuration control, pre-test checkout procedures, and post-test log data extraction.
Participate in configuration control board reviews for GNC software changes and maintain the software version log.
Support environmental qualification by preparing GNC software test configurations for vibration, thermal, and shock testing.
Provide GNC software technical inputs to subcontractor statements of work for GPS receiver and IMU firmware interfaces.
What You'll Bring
B.S. or M.S. in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Aerospace Engineering.
8 or more years of embedded flight software development for flight-critical defense or aerospace systems.
Expert-level C and C++ in real-time embedded environments including RTOS and bare-metal architectures.
Demonstrated experience implementing Kalman filter variants or flight control laws in embedded production code.
Proficiency in MATLAB and Simulink Model-Based Design including production C code generation using Embedded Coder or equivalent.
Experience developing or operating SIL and HIL test infrastructure for GNC algorithm verification.
Must be a U.S. citizen and eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.
Preferred Experience
Experience with GPS receiver software interfaces including NMEA, binary proprietary protocols, and M-code or SAASM pulse-per-second and timing interfaces.
Background implementing DO-178C, MISRA-C, or equivalent safety-critical software standards in a flight program.
Experience with high-g inertial sensor digital interfaces including SPI or UART IMU protocols and in-flight calibration algorithms.
Familiarity with MIL-STD-1553, RS-422, or ARINC 429 avionics bus interfaces.
Background with high-g avionics design considerations such as connector retention, PCB via-fill, and component derating under high-g launch load.
Experience with FPGA co-design for navigation algorithm pre-processing or sensor timing synchronization.
Active U.S. Secret or Top Secret security clearance.
What We're Looking For
An embedded GNC software engineer who can implement a navigation filter from a MATLAB prototype, make it run deterministically on a flight computer, and verify it against a 6-DOF plant model.
Someone who owns the SIL and HIL infrastructure, not just uses it, and can build it from scratch when it does not yet exist.
An engineer with the numerical instincts to know when a 32-bit float is not enough and the discipline to enforce coding standards that matter.
A technical leader comfortable reviewing algorithm equations with navigation engineers and debugging SPI bus timing issues with hardware engineers on the same day.
A high-ownership engineer who treats flight software as a safety-critical deliverable and builds accordingly.
Compensation & Benefits
Tiberius Aerospace offers competitive base compensation commensurate with experience, equity participation, comprehensive health benefits, and 401(k). Specific compensation will be discussed during the interview process.
Growth Opportunity
This role offers the opportunity to build the GNC flight software function at Tiberius Aerospace from the ground up on a program where the algorithm complexity and flight environment are genuinely challenging. The Senior GNC Software Engineer will own the implementation stack, build the test infrastructure, and close the software V&V against a real flight computer. As Tiberius grows, this person will be positioned to lead the broader flight software team and influence avionics architecture decisions on follow-on programs.

Define actuator bandwidth, slew rate, and torque requirements based on aerodynamic hinge moment data and closed-loop control performance requirements.
Develop gain scheduling logic for the full flight envelope and validate gain set transitions across

Participate in design reviews and evaluate engineering changes for stability and control impact.

8 or more years of flight dynamics and control law design experience on guided munitions, missiles, or high-performance aerospace vehicles.

Strong background in 6-DOF simulation and model integration for control law evaluation.

Experience with stability analysis and robustness verification under model uncertainty.

Background with ramjet or rocket-powered high-speed vehicle flight control design.
Familiarity with deployable or pop-out fin control surface design and hinge mechanism integration..

Active U.S. Secret or Top Secret security clearance.

ructural Analysis & Test Engineer

About Tiberius Aerospace

Tiberius Aerospace is a cutting-edge aerospace and defense company delivering advanced, mission-critical technologies for government and private-sector customers. We develop high-performance aerospace systems, secure engineering solutions, and complex hardware built for demanding operational environments.

Tiberius is scaling quickly and is seeking engineers who combine analytical rigor with a hands-on approach to building, testing, and qualifying hardware. Our teams move from concept to real hardware, test, and deployment with the speed and discipline required for high-consequence systems.

The Role

Tiberius Aerospace is seeking a hands-on Structural Analysis & Test Engineer to evaluate and validate the structural integrity, durability, and environmental survivability of mechanical assemblies and electronic hardware.

This role is analysis-forward, with direct ownership of structural verification and physical test support. You will translate system requirements and mission environments into component-level loads, analysis cases, verification plans, test conditions, and acceptance criteria. Your work will span static strength, fatigue, modal response, random vibration, shock, thermal-structural interaction, and qualification of flight-relevant hardware.

The ideal candidate is equally capable of building a credible finite-element model, checking it with first-principles engineering, defining a test approach, instrumenting hardware, interpreting the data, and turning results into better design decisions.

What You’ll Do

Structural Analysis & Verification

- Develop and maintain load flowdowns from system requirements to subsystems, assemblies, and components.

- Define load cases, interface loads, boundary conditions, factors of safety, margins of safety, and verification approaches appropriate to the hardware and operating environment.

- Perform static structural analysis of metallic structures, joints, fasteners, housings, electronic enclosures, printed circuit boards, and electromechanical assemblies using hand calculations and finite element analysis.

- Evaluate stress, deformation, stiffness, buckling, joint integrity, contact behavior, and structural margins.

About Tiberius Aerospace

Tiberius Aerospace is a cutting-edge aerospace and defense company delivering advanced, mission-critical technologies for government and private-sector customers. We develop high-performance aerospace systems, secure engineering solutions, and complex hardware built for demanding operational environments.

We are scaling quickly and seek people who operate with ownership, urgency, technical discipline, and sound judgment. Our teams work on real systems with real operational consequences—moving from concept to hardware, test, and deployment with speed and rigor.

The Role

Tiberius Aerospace is seeking a Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead the execution of complex aerospace and precision-strike hardware programs.

The TPM operates at the intersection of engineering, test, manufacturing, supply chain, quality, and program leadership. You will bring structure to complex technical work: defining execution plans, maintaining integrated schedules, managing risks and dependencies, driving accountability, and ensuring the team has the information and decisions needed to deliver.

This is not a status-tracking role. You will be embedded with technical teams, understand the product and its mission, anticipate issues before they become blockers, and help turn ambitious engineering objectives into flight-ready hardware.

What You’ll Do

Program Execution & Technical Leadership

- Lead the end-to-end planning, execution, and delivery of aerospace and defense hardware programs from concept through development, qualification, production, and field deployment.

- Build and maintain integrated program plans that connect technical scope, milestones, schedules, resources, risks, test activity, production readiness, and customer commitments.

- Partner closely with engineering leaders to define technical execution paths, clarify requirements, identify critical dependencies, and drive decisions.

- Manage the program’s cost, schedule, and technical-performance baseline, ensuring priorities remain aligned with mission needs and company objectives.

- Lead integrated program team meetings and establish clear ownership, action tracking, escalation paths, and decision cadence.

- Translate high-level product and mission requirements into actionable engineering workstreams and measurable deliverables.

- Drive execution across mechanical, structures, propulsion, aerodynamics, electrical, embedded software, flight controls, test, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain functions.

- Coordinate technical development activities from early design trades through prototype builds, qualification, flight test, and production transition.

Schedule, Risk & Dependency Management

- Develop and maintain detailed schedules, critical paths, milestone plans, and execution dashboards.

- Identify program risks, technical risks, resource constraints, and cross-functional dependencies early; establish mitigation plans and drive closure.

- Ensure configuration changes, design decisions, test results, supplier issues, and manufacturing constraints are reflected in program plans.

- Monitor program health using meaningful execution metrics, including milestone performance, test readiness, delivery predictability, issue aging, and risk exposure.

- Escalate issues with clear context, recommended decisions, and an understanding of the cost, schedule, and technical tradeoffs involved.

- Establish lightweight but rigorous processes that increase execution speed and accountability without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

Hardware Development, Test & Production Integration

- Work directly with engineering and test teams to plan prototype builds, integration activities, ground-test campaigns, environmental qualification, and flight-test events.

- Coordinate test readiness reviews, hardware availability, test instrumentation, data-review timelines, and follow-on corrective actions.

- Partner with manufacturing and supply chain teams to assess production readiness, supplier status, long-lead items, nonconformances, and delivery risk.

- Support engineering change, configuration-control, and design-review processes throughout development and production.

- Ensure lessons from test, field activity, and manufacturing are captured and incorporated into future builds and program plans.

Communication & Stakeholder Management

- Serve as a central execution interface between technical teams, executive leadership, external customers, suppliers, and program stakeholders.

- Deliver concise, accurate program updates that communicate progress, risks, decisions needed, and recovery plans.

- Prepare and maintain program artifacts including execution plans, schedules, risk registers, milestone reviews, technical status reports, and customer-facing materials.

- Support customer engagements by communicating progress, understanding mission needs, and ensuring commitments are incorporated into execution plans.

- Help create a culture of transparency, urgency, ownership, and disciplined technical delivery.

What You’ll Bring

- B.S. or higher in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Computer Science, or another relevant technical discipline.

- 5+ years of experience in technical program management, project engineering, systems integration, product development, or a related technical role.

- Experience supporting complex hardware programs in aerospace, defense, robotics, automotive, advanced manufacturing, or another high-consequence engineering environment.

- Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams through development, integration, test, qualification, and delivery.

- Strong understanding of the engineering product-development lifecycle, including requirements, design, integration, verification, test, manufacturing, and configuration control.

- Experience managing program cost, schedule, risk, dependencies, and technical deliverables.

- Strong judgment and the ability to understand technical tradeoffs well enough to drive decisions and unblock teams.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate technical information for executive, customer, and non-technical stakeholders.

- Proficiency with program-management tools such as Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Jira, Confluence, or equivalent.

- U.S. citizenship and eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with air vehicles, missiles, munitions, propulsion, flight hardware, aerospace structures, avionics, sensors, or other complex defense systems.

- Experience supporting DoD, national-security, or export-controlled programs.

- Experience planning and executing prototype, qualification, environmental, ground-test, or flight-test campaigns.

- Experience managing hardware production programs, supplier delivery, manufacturing readiness, and configuration-controlled releases.

- Experience with Agile, Scrum, Kanban, or hybrid engineering execution models.

- PMP, CAPM, Agile, Scrum, or comparable program-management certification.

- Experience with technical requirements verification and validation.

- Active U.S. government security clearance.

What Success Looks Like

You create clarity where there is ambiguity and momentum where there are blockers. You know how to ask enough technical questions to understand what is at risk, what decision is required, and what needs to happen next.

You are equally comfortable in a design review, at a build station, reviewing test readiness, or briefing the CEO. You do not simply report program status—you actively improve it. The teams around you have clear priorities, realistic plans, known risks, and the support needed to deliver.

Growth Opportunity

As Tiberius Aerospace scales through development and into full-rate production, this role will take on increasing ownership of major programs, customer commitments, and integrated product teams. The TPM will have a direct path toward Senior Technical Program Manager, Program Director, or broader operational leadership.
